claims.text: A PVD-applied TiN coating on a titanium alloy such as Ti-6Al-4V will increase surface hardness relative to the untreated alloy.
A PVD-applied TiN coating on a titanium alloy such as Ti-6Al-4V will increase wear resistance relative to the untreated alloy.
The untreated titanium alloy has moderate inherent hardness and wear resistance.
The proposed coating is a 3–5 μm TiN layer deposited by PVD.
The deposited TiN layer will be hard, dense, and well adhered to the alloy surface.
The TiN coating reduces surface plastic deformation because it is a hard ceramic.
The TiN coating acts as a barrier against abrasive wear.
The TiN coating acts as a barrier against adhesive wear.
A continuous and uniform TiN layer limits exposure of the titanium-alloy substrate to wear.
The coating will increase measured surface hardness by approximately 40–60% relative to the untreated substrate.
The coating will reduce wear rate by at least 50% relative to the untreated substrate in standard wear tests.
The hardness and wear improvements should hold at ambient temperature under standard mechanical loads typical of structural applications.
The predicted improvement may not persist at extreme temperatures, in highly corrosive environments, or when coating adhesion is compromised.
The magnitude of improvement depends on coating quality, uniformity, and PVD processing conditions.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant 40–60% hardness increase and at least a 50% wear-rate reduction is specified as the falsification outcome.
